data.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FINDING from the S1/S2 code now on the branch — record before this plan is reviewed, because the plan as written would regress an existing test.

S1 (7468, closed) made runner.run() resolution THREE-WAY: (a) a provider in ProviderSession._builders is EAGERLY built via infer_model(provider_factory=...); (b) a provider pydantic-ai recognizes but rebar does not build is left as a LAZY model STRING; (c) neither => typed LLMConfigError. Today _builders holds ONLY 'anthropic', so 'openai' takes path (b).

That matters because the openai SDK is NOT installed (verified: importlib.util.find_spec('openai') is None; rebar's [agents] extra deliberately omits it, and pydantic_ai.providers.openai raises ImportError at import). S1's implementer already hit this once: calling infer_model unconditionally broke tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py's parameterized 'openai:gpt-4o' case (line 358), which stubs _pai_structured precisely so no real provider is ever constructed. It was fixed by gating eager construction on supports()/is_resolvable().

So if S4 simply registers an 'openai' builder in _builders, supports('openai') becomes True and EVERY 'openai:...' model string — including ones with no base_url, and including that existing test — would take the eager path and hit the missing-SDK ImportError. The plan says the builder is 'gated behind the opt-in pydantic-ai-slim[openai] extra with a clear missing-extra error', which is right for the intended use but would convert a currently-passing test into a hard failure.

The plan needs to state which of these it does, because they are materially different: (1) register 'openai' only when cfg.base_url is set (base_url is the opt-in signal, and the plan already insists base_url is provider CONFIGURATION not SELECTION, so this does not make base_url a selector); (2) register unconditionally but have the builder fall back to pydantic-ai's own infer_provider when no base_url is configured, preserving path (b) exactly; or (3) register unconditionally and add the [openai] extra to the dev/test env, which changes rebar's dependency posture and should be an explicit decision, not a side effect.

Recommend (1) or (2). Also note S4 targets providers.py, which is at 225 LOC against the 300-LOC cap that is an ATTESTED acceptance criterion of closed story S1 — so the builder must be small or live elsewhere. And S4's line citation ':653' for _pai_check_config is stale after S1/S2; it is now at runner.py:718.
